decisions.title: Gift of Strength Repeat does not impose Powerstorm repayment
decisions.original_candidate_question: A Spirit with no Energy remaining receives Gift of Strength and has already used an eligible cost-1 Power Card. May it use that card's Repeat without paying its cost again, or does Gift require the same repayment as Powerstorm?
decisions.distinct_procedural_rule: A granted Repeat can impose eligibility without imposing repayment; Gift of Strength has no additional Energy payment.
decisions.source_correct_answer: Yes. The eligible Gift of Strength Repeat can be used with no Energy remaining. Its printed cost limit is an eligibility limit, not a payment instruction. Powerstorm’s separate explicit repayment condition does not apply to Gift.
minimum_asked_facts: The eligible Gift of Strength Repeat requires no additional Energy payment and may be used with zero Energy remaining.
decisions.source_backed_original_core_reachability: Gift of Strength is on the original Earth panel and explicitly grants this Repeat. The question stipulates an already-used eligible Power Card, not a foreign Repeat trigger. The no-Energy state is an ordinary legal resource state. No hypothetical modifier or excluded producer is imported.

printed_transcription.printed_text: Gift of Strength. Once this turn, Target Spirit may Repeat 1 Power Card with Energy cost of 1 or less. Instead, the Energy cost limit is 3 or less. Instead, the Energy cost limit is 6 or less.
printed_transcription.symbol_transcription: Fast, ANY Spirit. Thresholds: 1 Sun 2 Earth 2 Plant; 2 Sun 3 Earth 2 Plant; 2 Sun 4 Earth 3 Plant. No instruction to pay the repeated card cost again.

Elements for putting a Power Card in play, not for using its effect) and Repeats cannot be chained 
(ignore any “Repeat” effects on a Repeated Power). The Repeated Power is Slow or Fast, whichever 
the original Power is. Here are some additional fine points:
•	 Changes to a Power carry over to the Repeat use. (For instance, if a Power is made Fast or   
 given additional Range, that also applies to the Repeat.)
•	 You may make different choices when Repeating a Power.
•	 If a Repeat specifies where to use it, obey those instructions (instead of the usual Range and  
 Target restrictions). Otherwise, you can choose any valid target by the usual rules, including the

•	 Repeating a Power Card doesn’t count as playing another Power Card. (For, e.g., Boon of

decisions.title: Steady Regeneration permission, Growth limitation and per-disk price
decisions.original_candidate_question: When Green adds Presence via Growth, may it use destroyed disks while tracks still contain Presence? What is the price while Healthy versus Blighted? Does this special rule also let an ordinary Power Add Presence use destroyed disks?
decisions.distinct_procedural_rule: Steady Regeneration grants an optional destroyed-disk substitution specifically during Growth and prices each restored disk according to island health.
decisions.source_correct_answer: Yes, Green may use destroyed Presence for Growth even while its tracks still contain Presence. It is free with a Healthy island; with a Blighted island it costs 1 Energy for each destroyed Presence added. This special rule does not authorize an ordinary Power’s Add Presence to use destroyed disks.
minimum_asked_facts: Destroyed Presence may optionally supply Green’s Growth placements before tracks are empty.
This use is free while Healthy and costs 1 Energy per destroyed Presence added while Blighted.
Steady Regeneration applies to Growth, so an ordinary Power placement needs its own destroyed-Presence permission.
decisions.source_backed_original_core_reachability: The original Green panel supplies both the Growth placement and the explicit destroyed-Presence permission. Normal Blight can destroy Presence; Healthy and Blighted island states are standard core states. Green’s base Unique Overgrow in a Night is a real non-Growth Power placement producer (publisher account identifies it), so the final clause does not invent a Power action or imported effect.

printed_transcription.printed_text: ALWAYS... PLUS PICK ONE: When adding Presence to the board via Growth, you may optionally use your destroyed Presence. If the island is Healthy, do so freely. If the island is Blighted, doing so costs 1 Energy per destroyed Presence you add.

Optional groups: Reclaim Cards and Gain Power Card; OR Add Presence Range 1 and +1 Card Play this turn; OR Gain Power Card and +3 Energy. decisions.title: Stored Drowned Invaders may be exchanged outside the Drowning moment
decisions.original_candidate_question: Ocean has previously Drowned Invaders stored on its panel. Between actions in a later Spirit Phase, may it exchange them for Energy to help pay for cards that turn, or must it wait for another Drowning or the Gain Energy step?
decisions.distinct_procedural_rule: Drowning’s explicit exchange timing permits stored Invader conversion later, outside a Drowning event or normal income step.
decisions.source_correct_answer: Yes. Ocean can exchange the stored Drowned Invaders between actions in that later Spirit Phase and use the Energy for cards that turn. The printed at-any-time permission does not require another Drowning or the normal Gain Energy step.
minimum_asked_facts: Ocean may exchange stored Drowned Invaders at the stated between-actions time in the later Spirit Phase; it need not wait for another Drowning or the normal Gain Energy step.
decisions.source_backed_original_core_reachability: The original Ocean panel itself Drowns and stores Invaders and explicitly permits exchange at any time. Invaders moved into a board’s active Ocean are a normal core Drowning producer. The later stored-piece state and between-actions timing require no new external effect. The prompt does not ask interruption inside an unresolved action.

printed_transcription.printed_text: At any time you may exchange (X) Health of these Invaders for 1 Energy, where X = number of players. (Ignore modifiers to Invader Health.) Your Presence may add/move Presence into Oceans, but may not add/move Presence into Inland lands. On boards with your Presence, treat Oceans as Coastal Wetlands for Powers and Blight.
printed_transcription.symbol_transcription: Second Growth group has two Add a Presence in any Ocean instructions and +1 Energy. Third group has Gain Power Card, Push 1 Presence from EACH Ocean, and Range-1 Add Presence to Coastal land. Drowning region approximately [30,1490,1060,1710]; Growth [1020,20,2670,610].

source_evidence.passage:
If I gain an Element in the middle of resolving a Power, may I use that Element to gain a later threshold?
(.9v5kcmx)
Yes, you may.
This can happen, e.g., if the first part of
Indomitable Claim
reveals an Element on a Presence track, or if the land gets Blighted and the card is
Aid from Lesser Spirits
.
Likewise if you lose Elements in the middle of resolving the Power, you may lose further thresholds.
Note that any parts of the power that have already happened cannot be modified — those thresholds are either already hit or already missed. In particular, any thresholds that modify Speed or Range are checked first (before the rest of the power), and
~or~ choices are made before resolving either option
(.9v5kfqe)
.

Can the different thresholds of an innate power be used separately?
(.bu6od0c)
No, the thresholds are all part of a single power.  All effects must be used on the same target land (or same target Spirit), and you use the effects of every threshold you meet{1}, in the order they're printed{2}.
For example, Lightning's Swift Strike's innate power of
Thundering Destruction
used with 5 Fire, 4 Air, and 1 Water can destroy two buildings in the same land, but it cannot destroy two buildings in different lands. Even the final threshold on Serpent Slumbering Beneath the Island's
Serpent Rouses in Anger
targets a single land, although it affects all lands on the board in addition to the one that it targets.
One sort-of-exception: innate powers that say "Repeat this Power," like A Spread of Rampant Green's innate
Creepers Tear into Mortar
.  When a power is Repeated, you use the power from the beginning, which means you can target a new land.
{1} = You
are
allowed to pretend you have fewer Elements than you really do — e.g., to activate only the lower level of an innate — but that decision is made for the entire Power, not each threshold individually. Once you've chosen, you must activate every threshold those elements qualify for. Particularly, for Shadows Flicker Like Flames' innate power
Darkness Swallows the Unwary
, there is no set of elements which can activate the second threshold without also activating the first threshold.  If you destroy 2 Explorers to earn fear, you must first gather an explorer (if able).
{2} = Effects which modify Speed, Range, or targeting obviously apply when you check Speed / Range / targeting.
